pageCache.pageTitle: Good Shepherd Catholic Primary School - Catholic Life and Mission
pageCache.text:
Catholic Life and Mission
All of our children are involved in the Catholic Life and Mission of our school and we have two groups that are particularly focused on serving our school. They are our Faith Ambassadors and our School Councillors.
Our Faith Ambassadors help in two main ways — by offering ideas to enhance our worship (both in church and in school) and also putting their faith into action by helping others and supporting charities (such as The Catholic Children’s Society, Cafod, Missio etc).
In addition, our School Councillors help by improving our school environment (encouraging recycling, making the school ‘greener’ etc) and by sharing their ideas for improving other areas of school life. They are elected by their classes.
July 2026
As part of our exciting preparations for our new library, every child was invited to explore our existing book collection and choose some favourite books to take home. It was wonderful to see children leaving with armfuls of books, eager to continue their reading adventures at home.
The generosity didn't stop there. The remaining sixty bags of books, along with five bookshelves, were donated to a charity that will transport them to schools in Sierra Leone. We are delighted that our books will continue to inspire a love of reading in children across the world and look forward to seeing photographs of them being enjoyed in their new homes.
Diary Dates

pageCache.pageTitle: Good Shepherd Catholic Primary School - Ethos, Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Ethos, Vision and Values
Light, Life, Love
Light shows us the way
Love is the glue that holds everything together
Our children are very familiar with our Mission statement however we wanted to drill down to what it actually means to us and how it impacts on our lives. Each child gave their thoughts in words and pictures and together, from the whole school’s contributions, we have a clear representation.
Thank you in particular to Michael Soji, Sophie Lopez Jurado, Michelle Winner, Simona Pospisilova & Alfredo Tinajero-Webster for their words and Khea Mitchell for her imagery.
Light shows us the way Jesus’ light guides us to the path that leads to God.
Life is the way God created us for a reason: to serve Him, through serving one another.
Love is the glue that holds everything together. Love creates a stronger bond between us, holding us together as a Catholic family.
Jesus said, “I am the way and the truth and the life.”
Our Mission in Good Shepherd is:
To show Christian love for one another
To be attentive to one another
To live our lives following Jesus’ example

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Good Shepherd Catholic Primary School A message from the headteacher
Good Shepherd has developed significantly over the past ten years and it continues to do so, in order to meet ever-changing educational needs and to ensure pupils are equipped to meet life’s challenges in the knowledge that their Catholic faith will support their spiritual development on their journey.
The school is fortunate to have as its number one resource a high calibre teaching and support staff. Pupils, staff, governors and parents are extremely proud of their school and together make it a happy, caring environment, where everyone is valued and listened to and where together we strive to realise our hopes and expectations for all pupils.
I very much hope this website offers you a flavour of what we are about and we are more than happy for you to come and visit our school. If you require paper copies of any document on our website, please contact the school office.
Lisa De Souza Headteacher

Breakfast Club & After-School Childcare
Sugarplumz
We are a signpost for Sugarplumz, a provider of before and after school childcare.
Breakfast Club
In the mornings, Sugarplumz provides a breakfast club, based in our school. This is available from 7.30am until 8.45am, term time only. Children are given a nutritious breakfast and can enjoy a wide range of different activities in a safe and caring environment until school starts.
After-school childcare
Sugarplumz runs its after school club in the school too. After school club is available, term time only, up to 6.30pm.
Holiday clubs
In the school holidays, Sugarplumz runs a Holiday Club within Knights Temple Grove Primary School that operates from 7.30am until 6.00pm.
For more information, please contact Sugarplumz on telephone: 07415 109377, or by email: sugarplumz@hotmail.co.uk.

pageCache.pageTitle: Good Shepherd Catholic Primary School - Early reading - phonics
pageCache.text:
Early reading - phonics
Intent
At Good Shepherd Catholic Primary School, we believe that all our children can become fluent readers and writers. This is why we teach reading through Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised, which is a systematic and synthetic phonics programme. We start teaching phonics in Nursery/Reception and follow the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised progression, which ensures children build on their growing knowledge of the alphabetic code, mastering phonics to read and spell as they move through school.
As a result, all our children are able to tackle any unfamiliar words as they read. At Good Shepherd we also model the application of the alphabetic code through phonics in shared reading and writing, both inside and outside of the phonics lesson and across the curriculum. We have a strong focus on language development for our children because we know that speaking and listening are crucial skills for reading and writing in all subjects.
At Good Shepherd we value reading as a crucial life skill. By the time children leave us, they read confidently for meaning and regularly enjoy reading for pleasure. Our readers are equipped with the tools to tackle unfamiliar vocabulary. We encourage our children to see themselves as readers for both pleasure and purpose.
Implementation
Foundations for phonics in Nursery
We provide a balance of child-led and adult-led experiences for all children that meet the curriculum expectations for ‘Communication and language’ and ‘Literacy’. These include:
Daily phonics lessons in Reception and Year 1
Daily Keep-up lessons ensure every child learns to read
Teaching reading: Reading practice sessions and one-to-one reading
Additional reading support for vulnerable children
Ensuring consistency and pace of progress
Ensuring reading for pleasure
‘Reading for pleasure is the single most important indicator of a child’s success.’ (OECD 2002)
‘The will influences the skill and vice versa.’ (OECD 2010)
We value reading for pleasure highly and work hard as a school to grow our Reading for Pleasure pedagogy.
sharing high-quality stories and poems
attention to high-quality language.
decoding
comprehension: teaching children to understand the text.
Reception in Autumn 2
Year 1 in Autumn 1
Impact
Assessment is used to monitor progress and to identify any child needing additional support as soon as they need it.
As well as ongoing informal assessment, there are regular assessments to identify gaps in learning that need to be addressed, to identify any children needing additional support and to plan the support that they need.
Children in Year 1 sit the Phonics Screening Check and any child not passing the check automatically re-sits it in Year 2.

Daniel Hudson is the Clerk to the Governors
What does the Board of Governors do?
Our Board of Governors is established to oversee the running, management and leadership of our school.
Our Board of Governors includes:
Parent governors are elected by the parents of our school and normally serve for four years. Staff governors are elected by staff and normally serve for four years. Co-opted governors are invited onto the governing body, by the governing body, to add areas of expertise and to represent the local community.
The governing body is responsible for many important decisions in the running of the school.
Governors appointed by the Diocese (Foundation governors)
Teacher/support staff governors
Community or co-opted governors
Parent governors

You can contact the Board of Governors by emailing governors@goodshepherd.lewisham.sch.uk . Our governors are pleased to hear about thoughts, ideas and issues that staff and parents would like discussed by the Board of Governors. Individual governors can be contacted via the school office.
Full governing body meetings are held every half term in the evening. The agenda for the meeting includes items from the Local Authority, directives and initiatives from the Government and school-based concerns.

Parents' Evenings
During the Autumn Term and the Spring Term we hold two nights of Parents' Evenings where we offer the choice of 10 minute face-to-face or video-call appointments. Face-to-face appointments take place in the school hall in the first part of the evening and appointments by video-call take place virtually in the second half of the evening. Video appointments can be accessed on a laptop or mobile device. All appointments are booked online and parents are informed when the booking website goes live.

pageCache.pageTitle: Good Shepherd Catholic Primary School - Class Forums
pageCache.text:
Class Forums
At the beginning of each school year, we schedule Class Forums, when we invite parents into school to see their child’s classroom, meet the teacher and find out about the learning planned for that year. It’s an opportunity to ask questions about any aspect of your child’s teaching and learning, including homework, school routines, special events, school trips and so on.
The Class Forums take place in the classroom, starting at 9.00am and lasting for about 45 minutes. Attendance is not compulsory, but we do hope that as many parents as possible will use the opportunity to find out more about what their child will be getting up to in class and find out how best to support this at home.
Information shared during these sessions is uploaded to the school website so that any parents unable to attend in person can view this afterwards.
We promote dates for the Class Forums in the school newsletter so please look out for these at the beginning of each term.
